description: Send the traveller's current position to a navigation session and learn what to say. Pass `session_id` (from `start_navigation`), `lat`, `lon`, and when known `heading_deg` (clockwise from true north), `speed_mps`, `accuracy_m` and `timestamp` (RFC 3339; defaults to now; fixes must arrive in time order). HOW TO READ THE ANSWER: when `instruction_changed` is true, read `next_instruction` out (prefer its `landmark` phrasing, and its `direction`, "directly ahead, about 310 metres", when a heading was sent); when it is false, say nothing new. `state` is `on_route`, `off_route` (left the line but no reroute yet: a reroute needs 3 off-route fixes over at least 5 seconds, at most one every 10 seconds; `off_route.reroute_skipped` says why one did not happen), `rerouted` (a new route was computed from this position; `route` is present exactly then and `next_instruction` is its first turn), `arrived` (say so, then call `end_navigation`), or `lost_position` (the fix was not used, `fix.reason` says why: low_accuracy over 50 m, implausible_jump, far_from_route, out_of_order or after_arrival). `numbers_current` false means `distance_to_next_m`, `remaining_m`, `remaining_s` and `eta` are still the last accepted fix's, so do not announce them as fresh. `current_instruction` is the turn being made in the 20 m before it, when `next_instruction` already names the one after. Times are the engine's estimates. IF THE SESSION HAS GONE (it ends after 2 hours without a progress call, on `end_navigation`, and whenever the gateway restarts) this answers an error saying so: start a new session with `start_navigation` from the current position rather than retrying. Requires the MapMap gateway (GATEWAY_URL + GATEWAY_API_KEY); see /docs/navigation-sessions.

accuracy_m.description:
Horizontal accuracy the receiver states, metres. A fix worse than
50 m is not used.

heading_deg.description:
Direction of travel (or facing, on foot), degrees clockwise from
true north, 0 to under 360. With it, instructions carry a
`direction` phrased from where the traveller is.

lat.description: Latitude of the fix in decimal degrees (−90 to 90).

lon.description: Longitude of the fix in decimal degrees (−180 to 180).

speed_mps.description: Speed over ground, metres per second.

timestamp.description:
When the fix was taken, RFC 3339 (e.g. "2026-11-20T16:04:05Z").
Defaults to now, by this server's clock. Fixes must arrive in time
order.

name: check_navigation_progress

LatLon.description: A WGS84 coordinate in decimal degrees: a {lat, lon} object (preferred), or a GeoJSON [lon, lat] array with LONGITUDE FIRST, the same order as every polygon field on this server.

accepted.description: True when the fix was used for guidance.

reason.description:
Why not, when it was not: `low_accuracy`, `implausible_jump`,
`far_from_route`, `out_of_order` or `after_arrival`.

NavInstruction.description: One turn instruction of a navigation session.

direction.description:
Where it is from the traveller ("directly ahead, about 310
metres"), when the fix carried a heading. Read this out rather
than coordinates.

landmark.description:
Landmark phrasing ("Turn left just after the Co-op."), when
landmarks were asked for and one is recognisable there. Prefer it
when reading aloud.

step_index.description: Which step of the route this is.

text.description: The written instruction, e.g. "Turn left onto East Road."

verbal.description: The engine's spoken form, when it has one.

consecutive_fixes.description:
Consecutive off-route fixes so far (a reroute needs 3 over at
least 5 seconds).

deviation_m.description: How far the fix is from the route, metres.

reroute_skipped.description:
Why a confirmed departure did not reroute: `cooling_down` (at most
one every 10 s), `reroute_cap` (50 per session),
`no_waypoint_left`, `span_exceeded`, `not_reserved` or
`engine_found_no_route`.

NavRouteSummary.description: The route a navigation session is guiding along.

duration_s.description:
Travel time, seconds. On GB routes this includes the typical-delay
calibration described in `eta_calibration`.

eta_calibration.description:
The GB typical-delay calibration added to the travel time, the same
block as the `route` tool's: `applied`, `method`, `period`,
`engine_time_s`, `added_s`, `alternates_added_s`, `bands`,
`traffic_network_m`, `note`, `sources` and, on trucks, `truck_note`.
Absent when nothing was added.

geometry_polyline6.description: Route geometry, Google encoded polyline with six decimals.

steps.description: How many steps the route has.

version.description: 0 for the first route, one more for every reroute.

NavSnapped.description: A fix placed on the route.

course_deg.description: The route's course there, degrees clockwise from true north.

current_instruction.description:
The manoeuvre being made right now, in the 20 m before a turn
when `next_instruction` already names the one after it.

expires_at.description: When the session expires if nothing touches it (RFC 3339, UTC).

instruction_changed.description:
True when `next_instruction` is new since the last fix: read it
out. False: say nothing new.

next_instruction.description: The next manoeuvre. Read it out when `instruction_changed` is true.

numbers_current.description:
False when the distances and times are still the last accepted
fix's, because this one was not used.

remaining_s.description: Seconds still to go, the engine's estimate.

route.description: The new route, present exactly when `state` is `rerouted`.

snapped.description: The fix placed on the route, when it was.

state.description:
`on_route`, `off_route` (left the line, not yet a reroute),
`rerouted` (a new route was computed from this fix; `route` is
present exactly then), `arrived`, or `lost_position` (the fix was
not used; see `fix.reason`).
